svg.title: Quantum Fourier transform
svg.text: The quantum Fourier transform turns a number into dial angles
Four qubits hold the number 7. Gate by gate the transform turns each qubit's dial, until the dials stand at 7/2, 7/4, 7/8 and 7/16 of a turn.
Load the number 7 = 0111 (q0 is the highest bit)
q0: H makes it 0 and 1 at once
q0: halving turns of 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 from q1, q2, q3
q1: H makes it 0 and 1 at once
q1: halving turns of 1/4, 1/8 from q2, q3
q2: H makes it 0 and 1 at once
q2: halving turns of 1/4 from q3
q3: H makes it 0 and 1 at once
Swap q0 ↔ q3, q1 ↔ q2: now dial q stands at 7 ÷ 2^(q+1) of a turn
Inverse QFT: the dials fold back into 0111 = 7
Each qubit as a dial
hand = phase of the qubit's 1 against its 0, clockwise from 12 · no hand = a plain 0 or 1 · face: blue reads 0, orange reads 1
q0 (highest bit)
reads 0
turned 0
turned 7/16
turned 1/2
reads 0
q1
reads 1
turned 1/2
turned 7/8
turned 3/4
reads 1
q2
reads 1
turned 1/2
turned 3/4
turned 7/8
reads 1
q3 (lowest bit)
reads 1
turned 1/2
turned 7/16
reads 1
0×8 + 1×4 + 1×2 + 1×1 = 7. Plain 0s and 1s have no hands yet.
q0 read 0, so its hand starts at 0 (12 o'clock).
q1, q2, q3 read 1, so q0 turns a further 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16: now at 7/16 turn.
q1 read 1, so its hand starts at 1/2 turn.
q2, q3 read 1, so q1 turns a further 1/4 + 1/8: now at 7/8 turn.
q2 read 1, so its hand starts at 1/2 turn.
q3 read 1, so q2 turns a further 1/4: now at 3/4 turn.
q3 read 1, so its hand starts at 1/2 turn.
q0 7/2 → 1/2, q1 7/4 → 3/4, q2 7/8, q3 7/16 (whole turns drop out)
The angles held the number: undoing the transform reads it back.
Chance of each reading, with its amplitude as an arrow
bits = q0 q1 q2 q3, read as a binary number · arrow length is relative to the largest in that step
One reading is certain: 0111 = 7.
H splits each reading in two; the arrows carry the phases.
The chances stay put; only the arrows turn.
H splits each reading in two; the arrows carry the phases.
The chances stay put; only the arrows turn.
H splits each reading in two; the arrows carry the phases.
The chances stay put; only the arrows turn.
H splits each reading in two; the arrows carry the phases.
All 16 readings are equally likely, and each arrow is 7/16 turn past the one before it.
One reading is certain again: 0111 = 7.
